statement: The neuronal action potential is generated by voltage-gated Na+ influx (upstroke) and K+ efflux (repolarization) across a membrane whose ion gradients are maintained by the Na+/K+-ATPase; the Hodgkin-Huxley equations quantitatively describe and predict this membrane current.
effect_size: Quantitative model reproduces squid-axon membrane current; foundational, Nobel 1963
population: Squid giant axon (Hodgkin-Huxley); generalizes across excitable cells

provenance.primary: Hodgkin AL, Huxley AF - 'A quantitative description of membrane current and its application to conduction and excitation in nerve', J Physiol 1952
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-14 nervous-system brief; OpenAlex direct-search verified

confidence_notes: Foundation-tier, not outcome-tier. The Na+/K+ pump (Skou 1957, Nobel 1997) and Hodgkin-Huxley formalism are canon foundations under all downstream neuroscience.

statement: Microglia sculpt neural circuits by pruning synapses in an activity- and complement-dependent manner during development, and continue surveilling synapses in adulthood.
effect_size: Complement (C1q/C3)-tagged synapses engulfed by microglia; CR3-dependent pruning of retinogeniculate inputs

provenance.primary: Schafer DP, Lehrman EK, Kautzman AG, et al. - 'Microglia Sculpt Postnatal Neural Circuits in an Activity and Complement-Dependent Manner', Neuron 2012
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-14 nervous-system brief; OpenAlex direct-search verified

confidence_notes: Reframes glia as active circuit-shapers, not passive support. Mostly animal; mis-tuned pruning implicated in human disease but that link is hypothesis-tier.

statement: Astrocytes are active partners at the synapse (the 'tripartite synapse'): they recycle neurotransmitters, buffer ions, regulate blood flow and the blood-brain barrier, and (via aquaporin-4) drive glymphatic clearance during sleep.
effect_size: Glutamate uptake, K+ buffering, neurovascular coupling, AQP4-dependent CSF-ISF exchange

provenance.primary: Sofroniew MV, Vinters HV - 'Astrocytes: biology and pathology', Acta Neuropathol 2009
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-14 nervous-system brief; OpenAlex direct-search verified

confidence_notes: Direct bridge to Domain I glymphatic story. The 10:1 glia:neuron ratio is a myth (~1:1).

statement: Heart-rate variability indexes vagal/autonomic regulation and chronically low HRV associates with higher cardiovascular/all-cause risk, but HRV is a biomarker, not an intervention; 'raise your HRV' is not itself a validated health outcome.
effect_size: Association of low resting HRV with CV/all-cause risk; within-person interpretable only

provenance.primary: Shaffer F, Ginsberg JP - 'An Overview of Heart Rate Variability Metrics and Norms', Front Public Health 2017
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-14 nervous-system brief; cross-ref Domain I sec.4 + autonomic-HRV thread

confidence_notes: Predictor != lever. Noisy, posture/age/method-dependent. HRV-guided training as a real intervention is an open Wave-2 question. Cross-ref thread-autonomic-hrv.

statement: A bidirectional gut-brain axis links the enteric nervous system, gut microbiome, immune system and CNS via vagal afferents and microbial metabolites; manipulating the microbiome alters stress responses and behaviour in animals.
effect_size: Germ-free/altered-microbiome mice show changed HPA/behaviour; vagotomy blocks some effects

provenance.primary: Cryan JF, O'Riordan KJ, Cowan CSM, et al. - 'The Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axis', Physiol Rev 2019
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-14 nervous-system brief; OpenAlex direct-search verified

confidence_notes: Mechanism/animal strong; human 'psychobiotic' OUTCOME evidence thin, small, heterogeneous. Mechanism != outcome.

statement: Surgically implanted vagus nerve stimulation is FDA-approved for treatment-resistant depression (and refractory epilepsy), but the antidepressant effect is modest and slow.
effect_size: Modest response/remission in open and controlled studies; acute pivotal RCT was equivocal, benefit accrued over ~12 months

provenance.primary: Rush AJ, George MS, Sackeim HA, et al. - 'Vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) for treatment-resistant depressions: a multicenter study', Biol Psychiatry 2000
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-14 nervous-system brief; OpenAlex direct-search verified

confidence_notes: Real clinical VNS (device+surgery) is distinct from consumer 'vagus hacks'. Even here, depression evidence is modest and was contentious at approval.

statement: Midbrain dopamine neurons signal reward-prediction error (better-than-expected outcomes), the teaching signal of reinforcement learning; dopamine encodes motivation/learning, not pleasure per se.
effect_size: Phasic dopamine firing scales with prediction error; foundational to RL models of behaviour

provenance.primary: Schultz W, Dayan P, Montague PR - 'A Neural Substrate of Prediction and Reward', Science 1997
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-14 nervous-system brief; DOI from domain knowledge (OpenAlex rate-limited at verify time)

confidence_notes: Debunks 'dopamine = pleasure' pop framing. Underwrites the 'dopamine detox' debunk: you cannot reset baseline dopamine by avoiding fun; any benefit is behavioural stimulus-control, mislabelled as neurochemistry.

statement: There is no consistent evidence that depression is caused by low serotonin; the 'chemical imbalance' theory is not supported, though this does not negate the modest real efficacy of antidepressants.
effect_size: Umbrella review: no consistent serotonin-depletion association; SSRIs nonetheless beat placebo (SMD ~0.30, Cipriani 2018)

provenance.primary: Moncrieff J, Cooper RE, Stockmann T, et al. - 'The serotonin theory of depression: a systematic umbrella review', Mol Psychiatry 2022/2023
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-14 nervous-system brief; cross-ref Section 08 sec.5.3

confidence_notes: Mechanism story false; outcome (antidepressants work modestly) still true. Hold the two apart - the schema's central rule. Covered in full in Section 08.
dedup_note: Same finding as canonical claim 'serotonin-deficiency-myth' (Serotonin chemical-imbalance theory of depression unsupported); retained for chapter coverage, not counted as an independent claim.

statement: Constraint-induced movement therapy (restraining the unaffected arm to force use of the impaired one) improves upper-extremity function after stroke - plasticity harnessed clinically.
effect_size: Statistically significant and clinically relevant gains in arm function vs usual care at 1 year (EXCITE)

provenance.primary: Wolf SL, Winstein CJ, Miller JP, et al. - 'Effect of Constraint-Induced Movement Therapy on Upper Extremity Function 3 to 9 Months After Stroke: the EXCITE Randomized Clinical Trial', JAMA 2006
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-14 nervous-system brief; OpenAlex direct-search verified

confidence_notes: Real, RCT-grade neuroplasticity. Bounds the honest claim: adult plasticity exists and is trainable but domain-specific and effortful - not 'rewire your brain in 21 days'.

statement: Individuals do not have a dominant 'left brain' (logical) or 'right brain' (creative) hemisphere driving personality; hemispheric functional specialisation is real but no lateralized-network dominance distinguishes people.
effect_size: No evidence of whole-hemisphere connectivity dominance across 1011 subjects

provenance.primary: Nielsen JA, Zielinski BA, Ferguson MA, et al. - 'An Evaluation of the Left-Brain vs. Right-Brain Hypothesis with Resting State Functional Connectivity', PLoS ONE 2013
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-14 nervous-system brief; DOI from domain knowledge (OpenAlex rate-limited at verify time)

confidence_notes: Debunk. Hemispheric asymmetry (language usually left, spatial attention often right) is real; the personality taxonomy built on it is not. Companion debunks: 10% brain myth, 'rewire in 21 days'.

statement: Cognitive reserve - the capacity to tolerate brain pathology before showing deficits - is associated with education, occupational complexity and engagement; it is a strong predictor but a much weaker (and largely observational) lever.
effect_size: Higher reserve proxies associate with later/less symptomatic decline at equal pathology

provenance.primary: Stern Y - 'Cognitive reserve in ageing and Alzheimer's disease', Lancet Neurology 2012
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-14 nervous-system brief; DOI from domain knowledge (OpenAlex rate-limited); Scarmeas & Stern 2003 (10.1076/jcen.25.5.625.14576) verified

confidence_notes: Predictor != lever, and reverse causation is real (prodromal disease cuts engagement). What plausibly builds reserve is the sustained lifestyle bundle, not brain-game subscriptions (far-transfer fails).

statement: Placebo analgesia is a real neurochemical event: expectation of relief activates the brain's endogenous opioid system and is reversed by naloxone - demonstrating pain is a brain output modulated by context, not a fixed readout of tissue damage.
effect_size: Naloxone-reversible analgesia; mu-opioid receptor activation imaged during placebo (PET/fMRI)

provenance.primary: Amanzio M, Benedetti F - 'Neuropharmacological Dissection of Placebo Analgesia: Expectation-Activated Opioid Systems versus Conditioning-Activated Specific Subsystems', J Neurosci 1999
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-14 nervous-system brief; OpenAlex verified (also Petrovic Science 2002 10.1126/science.1067176; Zubieta J Neurosci 2005 10.1523/jneurosci.0439-05.2005)

confidence_notes: Core evidence for nociception != pain. The brain has a built-in opioid pharmacy that context dispenses.

statement: Chronic pain is best explained by a biopsychosocial model and central sensitisation, not by structural tissue damage; in chronic low back pain, imaging findings correlate poorly with symptoms and over-medicalisation is harmful.
effect_size: Disc/degeneration findings common in pain-free people; most low back pain has no identifiable structural cause
population: Chronic pain populations; Lancet Low Back Pain Series

provenance.primary: Gatchel RJ, Peng YB, Peters ML, Fuchs PN, Turk DC - 'The biopsychosocial approach to chronic pain: Scientific advances and future directions', Psychol Bull 2007
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-14 nervous-system brief; OpenAlex verified (also Hartvigsen Lancet 2018 10.1016/s0140-6736(18)30480-x; Treede Pain 2015 10.1097/j.pain.0000000000000160)

confidence_notes: Pain != tissue damage is the load-bearing modern fact. High-stakes correction: over-imaging/over-treating low back pain is iatrogenic.

statement: Pain neuroscience education (teaching that hurt does not equal harm) reduces pain and disability in chronic musculoskeletal pain, with small-to-moderate effects that are strongest when combined with exercise.

provenance.primary: Wood L, Hendrick PA - 'A systematic review and meta-analysis of pain neuroscience education for chronic low back pain', Eur J Pain 2018
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-14 nervous-system brief; OpenAlex verified (also Watson J Pain 2019 10.1016/j.jpain.2019.02.011)

confidence_notes: Concept well-supported; effect size modest and best with movement, not as a standalone lecture. Moseley & Butler 'Explain Pain' is the popularizer (provenance, not evidence).

statement: Diabetic peripheral neuropathy is prevented/slowed mainly by glycaemic control (clearly in type 1, modestly in type 2); its pain is treated first-line with gabapentinoids, SNRIs (duloxetine) or tricyclics - not opioids - but even first-line drugs help only a minority well.
effect_size: First-line neuropathic agents: number-needed-to-treat ~4-8 for 50% pain relief; common side effects
population: Adults with painful diabetic/peripheral neuropathic pain (systematic reviews)

provenance.primary: Finnerup NB, Attal N, Haroutounian S, et al. - 'Pharmacotherapy for neuropathic pain in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis (NeuPSIG)', Lancet Neurology 2015
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-14 nervous-system brief; OpenAlex verified (also Feldman diabetic neuropathy Nat Rev Dis Primers 2019 10.1038/s41572-019-0092-1; duloxetine Cochrane Lunn 2014 10.1002/14651858.cd007115.pub3)

confidence_notes: Neuropathic pain is genuinely hard to treat; NNT ~4-8 means most patients don't get major relief from any single drug. Managing expectations is part of treatment. Glycaemic control is the only disease-modifying lever and is largely upstream.
